segments.text: What is Integra Protocol?
Integra Protocol is a self-help method, a therapy technique and a spiritual tool developed by Vladimir Stojakovic.
It is simple and accessible to anyone, yet exceptionally efficient.
This new breakthrough in the field of self-improvement, therapy and spiritual development enables us to
resolve emotional problems,
release traumas and negative experiences,
increase our potential to achieve goals,
overcome negative beliefs,
accelerate our spiritual evolution.
Its main operating principle is
progressive integration of the unconscious content.
This principle we can also call
making the unconscious conscious.
Who can use Integra protocol?
Non-professionals looking to resolve their issues or reach higher states of consciousness,
and professional therapists, counselors, coaches, for their work with clients.
The core of our problems are internal conflicts that exist in every human being.
Integra Protocol teaches, step by step, how to integrate internal conflicts
in order to feel better, achieve your goals,
and dramatically accelerate your spiritual evolution,
all at the same time.
Integra Protocol System consists of three methods,
basic, standard, and advanced.
This digital seminar will teach you
how to apply all three Integra Protocol methods
on yourself as well as on others.

segments.text: Three topics of application.
We can apply Integra Protocol on three main topics.
Experiences, problems and goals.
What does it mean to apply Integra Protocol on an experience?
Let's say that I had a car accident 10 years ago, and when I think about it now, I feel anger.
This means that I still have emotional and mental charge tied to the car accident experience.
When I apply Integra Protocol on the car accident experience, I will release charge and from that point on, I will be able to think about the accident without negative emotions.
What does it mean to apply Integra Protocol on a problem?
Problems are automatic, compulsive reactions that always happen in the same situation or when we think about that situation.
For example, if my problem is fear of public speaking, I will always feel fear when I am speaking in public or when I think about it.
When I apply Integra Protocol on this problem, I will clear charge related to it and I will be able to speak in public without fear.
What does it mean to apply Integra Protocol on a goal?
Charge is also tied to our goals.
If I want to get fit, but feel resistance to exercise,
the resistance will prevent me from exercising, and I will not achieve my goal.
Charge prevents us from taking action, and if we don't take action, the goal will not be achieved.
When I apply Integra Protocol on this goal, I can release negative reactions associated with my goal, and I can bring myself into a state from which I can take action.
Every other topic that we can think of falls under these three, experiences, problems, and goals.
Clients often ask about beliefs. Are they a separate topic, or do they fit into these three?
They fit into these three. In their nature, beliefs are problems and in
Integra protocol they are treated as such. More about this will be in the
video, how to define topics.

segments.text: Identities. In the video titled Four Elements of Emotional and Mental Charge, we stated that there are only four different types of mind content. Images, thoughts, emotions and body sensations. If this is true, what are identities? Identities are not another type of mind content. They are thoughts and emotions we identify with.
Identities are of key importance for both resolving emotional problems and for spiritual development.
Let's talk about the importance of identities for the release of emotional problems.
When one says, I feel anger, that's different from, I am an angry person.
In the first case, I feel anger, one perceives the emotion of anger, which is a temporary state, and one knows it's temporary.
In the second case, I am an angry person, one is identified with anger and falsely perceives
that the identity angry person is one's true self and that this is permanent and unchangeable.
Exactly this is where our problems and suffering begin, when we identify with thoughts and emotions.
Negative thoughts and emotions are not a problem, we have capacity to deal with them.
Problems and suffering arise when we identify with thoughts and emotions.
Therefore, in order to eliminate emotional problems, it is of key importance to release stuck identities.
And releasing stuck identities is a key element of Integra Protocol.
Let's talk about the importance of identities for acceleration of spiritual development.
Spiritual development is the process of de-identification from the Ego.
Ego, the false self, consists of numerous identities in charge associated with identities.
Spiritual development, de-identification, happens when we make conscious and release stuck identities.
By de-identifying, our true self is gradually uncovered and we recognize that we are none of our stuck identities.
Identities and their totality that we call the ego are the reason for which spiritual
development was initially created and the reason for which it still exists.
Releasing identities, which is a key element of Integra Protocol, is a fast way to accelerate
your spiritual evolution.
We pointed out what is the nature of identities.
They are thoughts and emotions we identify with.
let's talk about the structure of identities. Structurally, an identity is a
point of view plus a goal that we want to accomplish from that point of view.
Knowing this enables us to release stuck identities. To release an identity we need
to assume its point of view and notice its goal. This will be further clarified
and demonstrated later in this seminar. Following are the examples of identities.
Point of view, an inferior person, with a goal to avoid attention and danger.
Point of view, suppressed person, with a goal to avoid falling apart. Point of view,
person who does not deserve respect, with a goal to do what I want without guilt.
Point of view, a sexual person, with a goal to avoid sex because I am insecure
about it. Point of view fallen person with the goal to send a message to others
look what you did to me. Point of view fearful person with the goal to provoke
mercy and be accepted. Point of view person in conflict with the goal to
avoid taking action. Point of view person obstructed by others with the goal to
have an excuse for giving up. Point of view a pretender with the goal to fulfill
expectations of others. Point of view person who waits with the goal to one
day live how I want.

segments.text: Progressive Integration. We talked about the four elements and identities. We mentioned that both our whole unconscious and our emotional issues consist of the four elements and nothing else. We also emphasized the importance of identities for both releasing emotional problems and spiritual development.
It's now time to explain what do we do with the four elements and identities in
Integra Protocol. Our main operating principle is progressive integration or
making the unconscious conscious. What does it mean making the unconscious
conscious? Often in life when we feel something negative we want to divert our
attention away from it. When using Integra protocol, we do exactly the
opposite. We direct our attention towards it, then we feel it, and then we verbalize
it. That is making the unconscious conscious. Direct attention, feel it,
verbalize it. Verbalizing means finding the correct words for the emotional
or thought. Verbalizing is the act of making something conscious. Once you find
the right words, the content or identity moves from unconscious to conscious.
Before it was something that you felt and now you know exactly what it is.
Making the unconscious conscious we also call integration. And why do we call it
progressive. Most of our problems are multi-layered, like cabbage or onion. It
is not enough to make conscious only one layer, because there are other layers
beneath the surface layer. Just as we would peel a cabbage until nothing is
left, we need to peel all the layers of our emotional problem until nothing is
left. We do this by repeating the above cycle direct attention, feel, verbalize,
going deeper and deeper until the problem is disassembled and released.
That's why I call it progressive integration. Progressive integration is
the main operating principle of Integra Protocol.

segments.text: Ability to assume and release identities.
We have an ability to assume any identity we need to achieve a goal,
as well as to release the identity once the goal is achieved.
In fact, without assuming an appropriate identity,
we couldn't do even the most basic daily activities,
or even perceive anything.
Throughout the day, we move from one identity to another,
realizing intentions, achieving goals, taking actions, and assuming different roles.
The process of assuming or releasing identities occurs unconsciously.
Moving from one identity to another usually happens quickly and easily.
In one of his books, Živorz Slavinsky gives the following example.
At work, one may have the identity of a medical doctor while seeing patients,
reading professional journals or discussing medical issues with
colleagues. When entering his car to go home he also enters the identity of a
driver. He adheres to traffic laws and avoids making mistakes while driving. At
home he assumes the identity of a husband. When he sees his children he
enters the identity of a father. Upon answering the phone to talk to his
mother, he is in the identity of her son and so on. Identities as such are not a
problem. Problems happen when we cannot assume the identity we need because we
are stuck in an opposite identity when we have an internal conflict. Stuck
identities are the problem. And how identities get stuck and create internal
conflicts more about this will be in the video internal conflicts

segments.text: Three Methods Intro.
Integra Protocol system consists of three methods, basic, standard and advanced.
In the book, Integra Protocol, How to Integrate Internal Conflicts, only the advanced method is presented, as it was the only one that existed at the time of writing the book.
However, all three methods are based on the concepts described in the book.
Basic Method.
Basic method is suitable for conflicted, stuck and complex clients.
It is also suitable when a person is very emotional and can only follow simple instructions.
Basic method is also good when you have limited time.
Basic method deals with only negative side of the conflict and only touches the positive side.
It integrates one stuck identity in one application.
It integrates the smallest quantity of emotional charge of all three methods.
In terms of spiritual experience, it raises awareness about emptiness, which is the essence of everything.

It integrates two conflicted identities in one application, and sometimes more than two.
It integrates the medium quantity of emotional charge of the three methods.

Advanced method

and for people who were progressively led to it
starting from the basic across the standard method.
Advanced method integrates a number of identities on both sides of the conflict
in other words it integrates multi-layered conflicts
it integrates the highest amount of charge of the three methods
In terms of spiritual experience, it raises awareness about presence, the state behind all identities, the state without identities, which is our true self.
It integrates high-level identifications.
It enters into very old and difficult-to-reach layers of unconscious.
It develops awareness of oscillations between the side in conflict.

on the level of the Being.

That is the only difference
between the two.
Identities and identifications
have the same structure:
they consist of a goal
and a point of view.
If they are stuck,

they both have their opposing
identity (or identification).
Most importantly,
they are both integrated
when we assume
their point of view
and recognise their goal.

Following are examples of
identities:

-point of view: inferior person
-with the goal: to avoid
attention and danger

-point of view: isolated
person
-with the goal: to turn to
myself

-point of view: person who
does not deserve respect
-with the goal: to do what l
want without guilt

Some examples of
identifications:

-point of view: consciousness
-with the goal: to maintain
awareness

-point of view: I
-with the goal: to exist

-point of view: Being
-with the goal: to have myself

-point of view: nothing
-with the goal: to fulfil
myself

-point of view: presence
-with the goal: to be aware of
myself

Why mention identifications
now?

Advanced Method goes
deeper
than the other two,
therefore it often results

in high level identifications
coming up.
We need to be aware of this.
Identities usually appear
in the beginning

and in the middle of the
process,
and identifications appear
towards the end.
The most important reason
for emphasising the difference

between identities and
identifications
is as follows:

when a beginner arrives at
identifications,

such as "consciousness", "I",
"being", "presence",
"emptiness", "nothing" and
similar,
he may assume

that he has completed the
process,
that he has reached the state

outside of identities and
identifications.

But, in many cases, that's not
true.

When it is true, it's the end of
the process.
When it is not true,

when we encounter high level
identifications,
they should also be integrated,

which means, we continue the
process.

When the client reports
identifications,
how do we know
is that an identification

or is that the end of the
process?
I will answer this question
a bit later in this video.

Now, when we know the
difference

between identities and
identifications,

let's discuss the technical
points of Advanced Method.

Advance Method has only one
new question.

Other questions from
Advanced Method

are also used in the other two
methods

and they are explained in the
relevant videos.
In this video,

I assume you are familiar with
them now.

Here, I will only discuss the
new question,
which is question number 4:

Feel (goal)... what happens?
(Image, thought, emotions,
body sensation)
For example:

Processor: From the point of
view of "able person", what is
your goal?
Client: To be independent.

Processor: Feel "to be
independent" and notice what
comes up?
Client: I feel fear.
The purpose of the question 4
is to activate more charge.
In the other two methods,

we are instructed just to list
goals,
not to feel them.
By feeling a goal,
as we do in Advanced Method,
we activate more charge,

which enables us go to
deeper.
By feeling the goal,
we take sides,

we support one side of the
conflict,

which provokes another
reaction,
hence, we get to go deeper.
Another reason

why we go deeper with
Advanced method
is as follows:

the other two methods have
stable points

and Advanced Method
doesn't.

Standard Method has the
emotion
as the first stable point,

and then it has the first
identity
and then the opposite identity
as stable points.
You stay for a while
with these stable points

which makes the process
easier,
but also more shallow.

Advanced Method has no
stable points,
and that's another reason
why it goes deeper.

The flow of Advanced Method
is simple:

Besides putting the definition
of the topic
in the proper format,

question 1 identifies the
content.
Since it is the topic definition,
it must be an emotion.
Question 2 identifies
the relevant identity

from which we perceive that
content.
Question 3 identifies
the goal of the identity.

Question 4 provokes the next
reaction,

which is content, (image,
thought, emotion or body
sensation).
And so on we continue:

content, identity, goal, content,
identity, goal...
in circles,
until we run out

of identities and
identifications,
and reach the state

without identities and
identifications.

That's what "Repeat 2-4 until
no more identities and
identifications appear" means.
We keep going in circles,
like a drill,
deeper and deeper,
until we make a hole
and reach empty space
on the other side.
As we keep going in circles,
we will shift

from one side of the internal
conflict
to its other side.

We might be in the "weak
person" identity
and then as we continue,

we shift into the "strong
person" identity.
The goal of Advanced Method
is to integrate all identities
that exist on both sides
of the internal conflict,
until we arrive
into the state of no identity.
This state of no identity
is the end phenomenon
of Advanced Method
and it will be
your biggest challenge
in learning Advanced Method
on your own.

It is challenging to recognise
this state

without having another
person
У

to guide you and tell you
"that's it"
But if you keep an open mind
and don't force it,
you will learn to recognise it.
And don't be discouraged
if you don't recognise it
in the first attempt.
Keep going.
When you guide other people
through Advanced Method
for the first time,

they should be notified
beforehand
that they would enter
a state without identities,
to expect it

as the normal end
phenomenon.
Note: when guiding someone

through Integra Protocol
methods
for the first time,

never start with the Advanced
Method.

You could start with Standard
Method,
but it is even better
to start with Basic Method.

Then, after they experience
Basic Method,
if it goes OK,
move to Standard Method.
And after a few times
with Standard Method,
if it goes OK,

you could move to Advanced
Method.

Even thought it is the simplest
method
of all three

and technically the easiest to
run,

Advanced Method is the most
demanding
for the client.
They need the ability

to verbalise a number of
identities
in one process.

Most people have no problem
doing it,
if they were progressively
and gradually guided,
starting from Basic,
across Standard,
to the Advanced.
I pointed out earlier
in this video
that when the client reports
high level identifications,
like "me",
"nothing",
"consciousness"
and so on,
it could be two things:

1. It is an identification and the
process should continue
2. It is the end of the process

The client reached the state of
no identity
and the client uses terms
like "me" or "consciousness"
to name the state somehow

even though there is no
identification.

How do we know the
difference?
It's simple.
If this state has a goal,
it's an identification
and if there is no goal,
it's the end of the process.
For example:

Processor: ... feel yourself...
what identity are you in now?

Client: Emptiness... 1 am
emptiness...

Processor: Feel emptiness..
From the point of view of
emptiness, do you have a
goal... or no?
Client: To fulfil myself.

In this case, it is an
identification.
The client has a goal,

and you should continue the
process
by moving to the question 4:

Feel "to fulfil myself"... what
comes up now?

Here is the same example
without a goal:

Processor: ... feel yourself...
what identity are you in now?

Client: Emptiness... 1 am
emptiness...

Processor: Feel emptiness..
From the point of view of
emptiness, do you have a
goal... or no?
Client: No, there is no goal.

In this case, it's the end of the
process.

Again, do not confuse an
identification
and the end of the process.
If there is a goal,
that's an identification.
If there is no goal,
it's the end of the process.

However, notice another
important detail here.
The previous only applies
to high level identifications.
It doesn't apply to identities.
Take this example:

Processor: ... feel yourself...
what identity are you in now?
Client: Angry person.

Processor: Feel angry person...
from the point of view of angry
person, what is your goal?
Client: There is no goal.

In this case, it's not the end of
the process
and we should continue.
Here is the same example,
including how to continue:

Processor: ... feel yourself...
what identity are you in now?
Client: Angry person.

Processor: Feel angry person...
from the point of view of angry
person, what is your goal?
Client: There is no goal.

Processor: What comes up
now?
Client: I feel frustrated.

Processor: Feel frustration...
feel yourself... what identity
are you in now?
Client: Powerless person.
Advanced Method finishes

in a state empty of emotional
and mental charge,

and this state is usually
preceded
by high level identifications.
Low level identities,
like "angry person"
indicate that the client
is still not close to the end,
so we continue.
Here is another mistake
practitioners often do
when using question 4:

Processor: ... feel yourself...
what identity are you in now?
Client: Persisten person.

Processor: Feel persistent
person... from the point of
view of persistent person,
what is your goal?
Client: To have success.
Processor: Feel success.
This is a mistake.

The client should feel "to have
success"
not "success"
There is a difference

between feeling "to have
success"
and feeling "success",

the difference between
wanting something
and having something.
To avoid this mistake,
in question 4 in particular,

and in Integra Protocol in
general,
never rephrase client's words.
Always use them exactly
as stated by the client,
without any changes.

Even when it is grammatically
incorrect,
or when you don't understand
what the client said.
This is important.
Verbalisation problems

There are two difficult aspects
of Integra Protocol:

confrontation and
verbalisation.
Confrontation means

that we have to face mind
content
that we would rather avoid.
Verbalisation means

that we have to find the
correct words
for that mind content.
Here is what we do

when the client is unable to
verbalise
the identity, content or goal.

-When the client is unable to
verbalise the identity:

Client: I feel an identity but I
cannot put it into words.

Processor: That's all right. Feel
that identity even though you
cannot verbalise it... from the
point of view of that identity...
through the eyes of that
identity... what is your goal?

-When the client is unable to
verbalise the mind content:

Client: I feel something but l
cannot verbalise it.

Processor: That's OK. Feel it
the best you can... feel
yourself... what identity are
you in now?

-When the client is unable to
verbalise the goal:

Client: I have a goal but l
cannot verbalise it.

Processor: That's all right. Feel
the goal and tell me anything
about it.

Client: It's like... when you
want other people to be
happy.

Processor: Feel "when you
want other people to be
happy"... what comes up now?

Advanced Method has only 3
questions
that we repeat in circles

and it is relatively easy to get
lost.
If you get lost
and you don't know
what is the next question,
simply ask:
"What comes up now?"

Take whatever they give you
and continue.

segments.text: Conclusion and Benefits. Now you completed the seminar and from this point on, if you use the methods, they will become a routine.
Depending on the charge you are dealing with, some processes will be easy and some will be emotionally difficult.
But remember, the more difficult the process is, the more emotionally liberating it will be.
As they say, the darkest hour is just before the dawn.
Sometimes, some practitioners are tempted to stop an emotionally difficult process.
This means losing a precious opportunity to release a big problem.
In times like this, remember the verse by Robert Frost,
The best way out is always through.
Once you realize, from your own experience, how true this verse is,
the more difficult the process is, the more determined you will be to go all the way and complete it.
Sometimes, especially at the end of the advanced method,
you will have some beautiful and precious spiritual experiences.
Once you experience them, you may want to repeat them every time.
Unfortunately, these beautiful experiences cannot be deliberately caused,
at least not at this stage of the development of the advanced method.
They happen when they happen. Enjoy them when they appear, but do not strive for them.
If you get stuck in a good experience, you compare it with other experiences of the same kind,
and you get unnecessarily disappointed with completely valid results.
Most participants of Integra Protocol Seminar are able to do all three methods
if they study them in the presented order.
However, some very small number of participants may have difficulties with the advanced method
or even with the standard method.
If this happens to you, it is completely ok to stay with the basic method for a while,
until it becomes easier.
Then you can move to the standard method and then to the advanced method.
Just stay with whatever is appropriate for you now, and soon you will be able to move forward.
There is nothing wrong with this approach and that's the main reason why we have three
methods.
How often should we do processes?
In my opinion, we should do them every day.
The best strategy is to commit to at least one process per day.
This way, you make a step every day.
And if there is a need to do more than one, or if you feel like doing more than one, you
can do as many as you need or like.
We can talk about benefits of Integra Protocol from at least two different perspectives.
One is quality of life and the other is spiritual development.
In our context, quality of life means feeling good and being functional.
They are two sides of the same entity.
When we talk about feeling good and being functional, we actually talk about problems
and goals.
On one side, emotional problems make us feel bad.
On the other side, being functional is our ability to work on our goals.
To bring it all together, we feel bad when some of our goals are unfulfilled.
Problems and goals are two sides of the same coin.
When I report a problem, for example, fear to approach women, I also have a goal, to
have a relationship or something similar. When I have a goal I have difficulties
with, for example, to have a relationship, I also have a problem associated with it,
for example, fear to approach women or something similar. Our emotional problems
are just barriers to our goals. This means the more emotional problems you
integrate with Integra Protocol, the better you feel. At the same time, the more emotional
problems you integrate, the more functional you will be, more able to work on your goals.
Because, to repeat, our emotional problems are just barriers, internal barriers, to our
goals. Both benefits, feeling better and becoming more functional, are happening at the same
time as you release your emotional problems. And this will contribute to
your quality of life since when we want something it's either to feel better or
to achieve something depending which side of the coin you are thinking about at
this moment. The other benefit of using Integra protocol which is also happening
at the same time is spiritual development as mentioned earlier in this seminar
Spiritual development is just disidentification from various false identities.
And with its continuous use of disidentification,
Integra Protocol accelerates your spiritual evolution dramatically.
Another benefit is independence and the fact that you don't have to suffer negative states,
whether they are connected to experiences, problems or goals.
Knowing Integra Protocol methods, you can use the first opportunity to apply them and release the current negative state.
Another benefit, as you gain experience with Integra Protocol, you will become aware of the kind of situations in which you create charge.
and when those situations come up in everyday life,
you will recognize them,
which will reduce the amount of emotional charge that you create.
So it's not just that you are releasing charge now,
but you also create it less.
The average human being carries a great burden.
When we do a process,
we invest both in the present and in the future.
Firstly, we no longer feel the negative state that bothered us just before the process.
Secondly, our burden, the total weight we carry, will be lighter tomorrow for the amount of charge we integrated today.
And this will result in a better quality of life and the gradual liberation of consciousness from the shackles of the ego,
what is commonly called spiritual development.
Our erroneous perception that identities are our true being
creates suffering.
At the end of each advanced method,
one experiences oneself without identities,
becomes more aware of one's true nature
and regains wholeness,
while the number of stuck identities is reduced.
This identifying from stuck identities will result in gradual recognition of the Self as a non-material and immortal being, inseparable from the rest of existence.
I wish you many adventures on your spiritual journey.
